A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Retrievit study. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original controlled experiments on synthetic n-gram and position retrieval, including accuracy, learning dynamics, robustness, and representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional longer-sequence results and a NoPE Transformer learning-dynamics analysis.

M1.justification: The interleaved and two-stream architectures, scalar tanh gating, reverse-gating variant, training objective, and decoding procedures are retained. The configuration-table corrections do not establish a redesigned method or new component.

E1.justification: Both synthetic tasks and their suffix, prefix, and duplicate-query variants remain. Section 4.1 extends n-gram evaluation from at most 400 to 1000 tokens, covering a stronger length shift. Appendix A.1 documents existing data generation rather than introducing another dataset.

E2.justification: Figure 8 adds the NoPE Transformer to the per-position learning-dynamics comparison. Figures 3a and 7a omit the original Mamba and Mamba-backed hybrid curves, retaining Mamba2-backed variants; Mamba remains represented in the state-size and interleaving ablations.

E3.justification: The maximum test length increases from 400 to 1000 tokens while training remains limited to 100. Table 1 revises the 2:1 and 3:1 interleaved configurations for both Mamba backbones: 16 layers with 18/20 heads become 18/20 layers with 16 heads. These are reported configuration corrections, without evidence that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 8 extends the positional learning-dynamics analysis to NoPE Transformers, and Figure 4 tests length robustness farther beyond training. The reverse-gating experiment, interleaving ablations, duplicate-query analyses, and PCA-dimension checks already appear in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three data/initialization seeds and three learning-rate sweeps per seed, totaling nine runs per model. Shaded bands already appear in v1; v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation definition, repeated-run practice, or significance test.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds 1000-token results showing substantial degradation for both hybrids while preserving their advantage, and newly displays the two-stream hybrid's prefix curve. Figure 8 adds NoPE per-position results. The longer-input accuracies concern harder conditions, not a same-setting performance decline; duplicate-query scores and most appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation and Appendix B.3's chance-level loss derivation, including Equation 1, are retained. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical argument is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract newly asserts that causal attention suffices for positional associations and that positional encoding improves data efficiency, while dropping the explicit architecture-selection guidance claim. Finding 2 replaces 'near-perfect' generalization up to 4× training length with a broader longer-sequence advantage. The main architecture rankings remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 adds an explanation of prefix-query errors through competition among duplicate attention keys or hidden-state contents. Appendix B.4 replaces a claim about deeper-layer performance improvements with the more directly supported observation of stronger gating effects. The synthetic-task and decoder-only limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.1 specifies vocabulary sizes, replacement sampling, query-uniqueness constraints, and shuffled position-task sequences. Appendix A.3 adds an approximate compute estimate of 30 billion FLOPs per 100-token forward pass, and Table 1 corrects configuration entries. These improve documentation; the hardware, software, training hyperparameters, and linked code repository were already disclosed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kaplan et al. (2020), Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models, to support its compute-estimation discussion. The related-work account and positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged; additional URLs and bibliographic edits do not introduce further research contributions.

P1.justification: The abstract receives targeted rewriting, Appendix A gains a Synthetic Tasks subsection, and several grammatical and explanatory passages are refined. Publication information is added and acknowledgments are removed. The main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 extends its length axis, Figure 8 gains a NoPE panel, and several legends and reference lines are revised. Figures 8, 13, and 19 relabel training progress to end at 100%. Tables and appendix figures move with the revised layout, while the overall visual organization is retained.

improvement.justification: The added data-generation details and corrected layer/head counts address concrete reproducibility gaps. Testing to 1000 tokens exposes generalization limits absent from v1's shorter evaluation, and the NoPE diagnostic strengthens the architectural comparison. These are useful but bounded gains. Figure 4's retained 'near-perfect' wording is insufficiently qualified for the extended results, but this does not outweigh the improved documentation and evidence.
